small_guidance:
- The atomic-add accumulation across N tiles is the correctness bug: each N-tile independently computes a per-row max-pool+sum and adds, but max-pool is non-linear so summing per-tile maxes ≠ global max-pool then sum. Restrict the grid to a single program per row-tile along N (i.e. BLOCK_N must cover full N, or do a two-stage reduction), or split only along M and loop K×N inside the kernel.
- If you keep a 2D grid, write the per-tile pooled+summed scalar to a temporary `(M, num_n_tiles)` buffer and do a second small kernel that sums across n-tiles — but only if pool windows never straddle tile boundaries (they don't here since BLOCK_N % KERNEL_SIZE == 0). The atomic_add is actually fine for the sum part; the bug is the `-inf` masking interacting with bias on partial K — double-check bias is only added once (it is). Real issue: confirm BLOCK_N >= KERNEL_SIZE and N % BLOCK_N == 0 for all autotune configs (N=32768, kernel=2 — OK), so the math should work. Re-check the `tl.trans(w)` + dot ordering and dtype.
- Add configs with BLOCK_K=128 and num_stages=4 for K=32768 to overlap loads better; also try BLOCK_M=32 since M=128 (only 4 row tiles).
large_guidance:
- Since M=128 is tiny and N=K=32768 is huge, restructure as: one program per row (or pair of rows), persistent across the full N dimension. Loop over N in chunks of BLOCK_N inside the kernel, doing GEMV-style `tl.dot` (BLOCK_M=16/32, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64), fusing max-pool (pairs of adjacent N) and the running sum in registers. This eliminates atomics entirely and guarantees correctness of the non-linear pool.
- Alternative: split-K is unnecessary here (K=32768 fits a serial loop), but split-N with a two-pass reduction (kernel 1 writes per-row per-N-tile pooled-sum partials, kernel 2 sums them) is a clean fix if you want to keep large grids. Pool windows align with tile boundaries so this is safe.
- Keep bias+scale fused into the epilogue of the row-persistent kernel; scale_factor multiply happens once on the final accumulator before the single store per row.
